floor: Every student completes the regular-level standard (T6): name the metal from its flame color, and say what the flame cannot decide. Bands (hidden) change hint depth and the supply of extra unknowns only. Nothing sits above the standard.

clock.note: Lab day: huddle 2 comes after the data, not at minute 25. Exit ticket 39-42.

gates.huddle1Code: the door stays shut until the pre-lab is done (existing lab-01 mechanic); code 1 is given by Mr. D at the end of huddle 1
gates.huddle2Code: accepted only when the lab record is complete: seven flame tests recorded, both unknowns answered. A student who is not done sees nothing to enter and needs Mr. D. PENDING: this conflicts with CLAUDE.md's one-code rule and needs Mr. D's confirmation.

questions.picture: a + circle and a - circle with a gap between them
questions.q: Do these two charges attract or repel?

questions.picture: a nucleus with one electron on shell 1 and one on shell 3
questions.q: Which electron is held more tightly?
questions.explain: Shell 1 is closest to the nucleus, so the pull is strongest.

questions.picture: two charges 1 unit apart, then 2 units apart
questions.q: At 2 units apart, is the force stronger or weaker?
questions.explain: Farther apart means a weaker force.

prediction.q: Will NaCl and NaNO3 burn the same color?
prediction.afterTry: Good. You will test this in the lab.
prediction.note: Do not reveal the answer here. The lab shows it.

quests.text: Put on goggles and an apron
quests.hint: Walk to the LOCKER and press E. Choose Put on for the goggles and the apron.

quests.text: Go through the door into the lab
quests.hint: The light on the DOOR turns green when you are geared up.
It is the bench with the burner. Face it and press E. The seven salt bottles and the splints are already there; you do not carry them.

quests.text: Test NaCl: dip a fresh splint, hold it at the edge of the flame for 10 seconds
quests.hint: Pick a fresh splint, dip it in the NaCl bottle, then hold it at the flame edge. Watch the timer ring.

quests.text: Record the color and the brightness in your table
quests.hint: Open your notebook and fill the NaCl row. The swatch and the color name sit side by side.

quests.text: Test the other five salts and NaNO3
quests.hint: One fresh splint each time. If the flame flashes yellow, you reused a splint.

quests.text: Take unknown bottles A and B from the UNKNOWNS shelf
quests.hint: You can carry six. Take only A and B.

quests.text: Flame-test A and B and record them
quests.hint: Compare each color with your known table.

quests.text: If two knowns match, use the spectroscope
quests.hint: It sits on the FLAME BENCH. Open it with E and look at the flame.

quests.text: Choose an identity for each unknown, or say you cannot tell
quests.hint: There is no answer check, so retest before you submit.

quests.text: Write your claim, evidence and reasoning
quests.hint: Use the starters. Your evidence is your own table.

tests.name: Flame test
tests.how: Dip a fresh splint in the salt, hold it at the edge of the flame for 10 seconds, and record the color and the brightness.

tests.name: Spectroscope
tests.how: Look at the flame through the spectroscope. Each bright line is one color of light. Record where the lines fall.

postlab.prompt: Choose one of your unknowns. Which metal is it, or which two could it be, and how do you know?

claim: Unknown __ is either ___ or ___, and I need a second test.
reasoning: This evidence supports my claim because
The flame cannot decide between ___ and ___ because

checklist: My claim answers the question in one sentence.
My evidence is the color I saw in my own table.
If two metals matched, my claim says so.
My reasoning says why the evidence points to that metal.

exit.prompt: Draw three energy levels for an atom. Show an electron dropping from level 3 to level 1 and a second, smaller drop. Draw the light that comes out of each and label which one is bluer.
look: levels are separate lines, higher means more energy
arrows go from higher to lower
the longer drop is the bluer light

homePractice.prompt: This flame is yellow-orange. Which known metal does it match?
hints: Open your table. Find the row whose color says yellow-orange.
Read down the color column until you see yellow-orange. What metal is in that row?
Another case: a blue-green flame matches the row that says blue-green. Do the same with yellow-orange.

homePractice.prompt: This flame is orange-red. Which known metal does it match?
hints: Use your table, not memory.
Find the row that says orange-red.
Compare the swatch with each color in your table. Which swatch is the same?

homePractice.prompt: NaCl and NaNO3 both burn yellow-orange. What sets the flame color?
hints: Look at what NaCl and NaNO3 have in common.
The two salts have different second parts. What is the same in both?
Another case: the same red paint on a door and on a wall. The color comes from the paint, not from the thing it covers. Which part of each salt plays the role of the paint?

homePractice.prompt: A student says the chlorine in NaCl makes the yellow color. Which result in your table shows this is wrong?
options: NaNO3 has no chlorine and is also yellow-orange
homePractice.answer: NaNO3 has no chlorine and is also yellow-orange
hints: The student's claim is about chlorine. Which test has no chlorine?
Find the salt in your table that lacks Cl.
To test a claim about one part, change only that part and see whether the result changes.

homePractice.prompt: You see a lilac flame. Which metal is it, and why might yellow hide it?
options: K; sodium's bright yellow can mask it
Cu; the yellow is the splint
homePractice.answer: K; sodium's bright yellow can mask it
hints: Look up lilac in your table.
Now look at how bright sodium is compared with that metal.
Another case: a dim light next to a very bright one is hard to see. Which flame is the dim light here?

homePractice.prompt: The flame shows a yellow flash, then lilac. Which metal are you burning?
options: K, with a little sodium on the splint
homePractice.answer: K, with a little sodium on the splint
hints: Which color lasted?
The color that lasts is the metal. The flash is something extra.
Another case: a quick yellow flash from a splint is sodium, not your sample.

homePractice.prompt: Which two metals could you mix up if you used only your eyes?
hints: Look for two rows with the same color name.
Read the color column again. Which two match?
Rows with identical swatches look identical. Find the identical swatches.

homePractice.prompt: A spectroscope shows one yellow line at 589 nm. Which metal?
hints: Find the yellow region of the strip.
Which metal's row has a line at the yellow position?
Another case: a blue line near 461 nm points to the row that has a blue line. Do the same with yellow.

homePractice.prompt: An unknown burns crimson. Your knowns include Li and Sr, both crimson. Which claim is true to the data?
options: It is Li or Sr; a second test is needed.
homePractice.answer: It is Li or Sr; a second test is needed.
hints: How many known metals match crimson?
If two metals match, can the color alone choose between them?
Another case: two keys fit the same lock. The lock alone cannot tell you which key you hold.

homePractice.prompt: A spectroscope shows a bright red line near 671 nm and a dimmer orange line near 610 nm. There is no blue line. Which metal?
hints: Check each row of the strip for a blue line.
Which of Li and Sr has a blue line?
Another case: Na has one yellow line and no blue line. Decide the same way for these two.

homePractice.prompt: A spectroscope shows a blue line near 461 nm plus red lines. Which metal?
hints: Find the blue region of the strip.
Which crimson metal has a blue line?
The blue line is the difference between the two crimson metals.

homePractice.prompt: In one sentence: what can the flame test not decide?
homePractice.grading: PENDING (decision for Ian): self-compare with the model answer, or you read it
homePractice.modelAnswer: It cannot separate metals that burn the same color, such as Li and Sr.
hints: Think about the Li and Sr rows.
Finish: The flame cannot decide between metals that ___.
Another case: two shirts of the same color cannot be told apart by color.
